Courtland Sutton draws a plus matchup — JAX concede 68 yds/game to WR1s (league ~58), and DEN funnel 23% of targets his way. A rec-yards spot.

The DEN host the JAX as favorites of 3.0, with the total set at 43.5 — a market that implies a DEN 23–20 scoreline. Running the game forward from that baseline, we expect a contest that spends roughly 31% of its snaps with DEN in front, 41% within one score, and 27% with DEN chasing. That distribution is the engine of everything below: game state is what turns a team's tendencies into a specific player's workload, so before we get to individuals it's worth being explicit about how this game is likely to be played.

This is a coin-flip script. With only 3.0 points separating them, neither team projects to spend much time in a blowout state — most of the game lives in the 'close' bucket, where play-calling stays balanced and usage tracks each player's established role rather than being distorted by score. In tight games the stars on both sides see their normal, dependable workloads, and there is less garbage-time leakage to backups.

The Key Matchups

Tough sledding for J.K. Dobbins — JAX are stingy against the run (109 yds/game, well below the ~120 norm); lean under on his rushing line.

Tough sledding for Chris Rodriguez Jr. — DEN are stingy against the run (102 yds/game, well below the ~120 norm); lean under on his rushing line.

Bo Nix has a passing-yards tailwind — JAX allow 252 pass yds/game (vs ~230).

Sneaky value on Jaylen Waddle (WR2) — JAX leak 44 yds/game to the WR2 role, above the ~36 norm.

Touchdown Board

Evan Engram is a live anytime-TD dart — JAX are leaky to tight ends in the end zone (0.31 TE TDs/game vs ~0.24).

DEN — a balanced offense

DEN are a balanced offense — their run/pass split by game state tracks the league closely (43% pass when leading vs 44% average), so their players' usage is driven more by role than by any strong situational lean.

J.K. Dobbins (13 carries, 62 yards) projects to his baseline workload — no strong script push either way in a close game.

Courtland Sutton projects for 6 targets and 50 yards, in line with his established role in a script that neither inflates nor suppresses the pass.

What to watch

The single biggest swing factor is availability — use the injury tool in the sidebar to mark anyone out; a starter's absence doesn't just remove his line, it redistributes his targets and carries to specific teammates, and the report and projections rebuild around it. Beyond that: if this game breaks toward the projected 3-point margin, the garbage-time backups (the ◆-flagged rows below) are where soft lines and real edge tend to appear — those depth players get fed in blowouts, and the market is slowest to price them.
